title: GB-0669, an AI-designed anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody, completed a randomized first-in-human trial
summary: Phase 1 of the AI-designed antibody GB-0669 in 51 healthy adults showed tolerability, a 54-day half-life and dose-dependent virus neutralization.
account: Generate Biomedicines designed GB-0669 using machine learning. It is a monoclonal antibody against the conserved SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 stem helix. A phase 1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled single-ascending-dose trial, registered as NCT07050511, enrolled 51 healthy adults. 36 received GB-0669 and 15 placebo, across five dose cohorts from 100 to 2,400 mg. The trial ran from 18 July 2023 to 22 November 2024. The results were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases on 14 July 2026. No dose-limiting toxicities occurred, and all adverse reactions were grade 1 or 2. Pharmacokinetics were dose-proportional with a 54-day half-life. Dose-dependent serum live-virus neutralization occurred at 600 and 1,200 mg. No patient benefit was demonstrated, and the authors propose phase 2 evaluation in immunocompromised patients.
purpose: Use generative machine learning to design a therapeutic antibody against a conserved, poorly immunogenic region of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.

ratings.reason: The trial enrolled healthy volunteers and measured safety, pharmacokinetics and serum neutralization; no person obtained a therapeutic benefit.
The source reports a completed phase 1 and a recommendation to proceed to phase 2, not a realized organizational outcome.
No population-level benefit is demonstrated; the antibody has not been shown to prevent or treat infection in patients.

ai_role.statement: The antibody itself was AI-designed and optimized against the spike S2 stem helix, so the AI output is the investigational product. The in-human findings are safety, pharmacokinetic and neutralization measurements from a randomized placebo-controlled trial, not evidence of clinical benefit. The peer-reviewed report is written by the developer's staff. The independent corroboration available is the trial registry record.
